description: Tier 1, the baseline problem. Hostiles arrive one at a time from the perimeter and transit toward the asset; civilian traffic crosses the same airspace on straight lines at a similar speed. Everything is visible to somebody at some point and the radio is clean. The whole difficulty is telling a threat from a bystander and paying one drone per kill and not two.
_evasion: A hostile weaves once an interceptor is inside 40 m. The amplitude here, 3.5 m/s^2, is deliberately about half of an interceptor's lateral authority, which is g*tan(max_tilt) = 6.7 m/s^2 and not max_accel. At the published default of 8 m/s^2 the hostile out-turns the interceptor and the endgame cannot be flown by anybody, which is not the thing tier 1 is supposed to be testing. Fitting the manoeuvre is tier 7's job.
_fleet: Sixteen against six, not twelve. The weapon is the airframe, so every interception spends one: a fleet of twelve that stops all six arrivals is a fleet of six by the end, holding a ring it was spaced for at twelve, with the gaps between neighbours twice what the sensors can cover. Measured across tier 1, that is where the leak was - not the first arrival, which is met by a full formation, but the fifth or sixth against a picket with holes in it. A fleet has to be sized as the ring plus one drone per hostile, and the ring is what the radio and the sensors say it is.
